# Connecticut local moratoria

Every local infrastructure moratorium in the inventory for Connecticut, current through **August 19, 2026**.

**4 instruments** — 2 in force, 1 pending, 1 past.

State policy is tracked separately: **7 actions** (7 bills) in [`state_legislation.csv`](../data/state_legislation.csv). These are not included in the local count above.

## Detailed entries

### Groton

- **Type:** Town
- **Status:** ⚪ Replaced
- **Date enacted:** 2022-06-14 (Groton PZC adoption, 5-0 vote); effective 2022-07-15, per the adopted motion text in the June 14, 2022 PZC meeting minutes: "This text amendment shall become effective July 15, 2022."
- **Normalized date:** `2022-06-14` (exact)
- **Duration:** One year
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `ct-groton-2022`
- **Legal basis:** Planning and Zoning Commission application REGA22-01, Data Center Moratorium Text Amendment, town-wide
- **What prompted it:** Local proposals for large data centers, uncertainty about how data centers differed from telecommunications facilities, and resident concerns about noise, stormwater, generator use, energy use, and environmental impacts
- **Affected projects:** Data center applications; public reporting states the pause applied to developments larger than 5,000 square feet and followed proposals for two 250,000-square-foot facilities near Interstate 95
- **Detailed status:** Replaced
- **Outcome:** Permanent regulations adopted in 2023 limit principal data centers to 12,500 square feet and impose siting and operating limits; public reporting describes this as blocking hyperscale projects

### Morris

- **Type:** Town
- **Status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** The identical moratorium text (prepared by the Town Planner and dated 2026-03-23) was re-filed by the Commission under its 'regulations' folder -- rather than the earlier 'generals'/draft-agenda-attachment folder it occupied as of the April 15, 2026 meeting -- under the title 'Public Hearing Two Year Moratorium on Battery Storage Facilities and Data Centers,' with a document date of 2026-05-20. Secondary reporting describes a public hearing held on a Tuesday and Commission approval the same week, consistent with adoption around 2026-05-19/20. Neither the exact adoption-vote date nor the Connecticut-statute-required newspaper publication date (which triggers legal effectiveness) was found in any source I could access.
- **Normalized date:** `2026-05` (month_only)
- **Duration:** 12 months from effective date of adoption
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** battery storage, data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `ct-morris-2026`
- **Legal basis:** Town of Morris Planning and Zoning Commission, Zoning Moratorium on Battery Energy Storage Systems and Data Centers
- **What prompted it:** Need to evaluate land use, environmental, infrastructure, fire safety, emergency response, groundwater, traffic, noise, visual, electrical infrastructure, and water-use impacts
- **Affected projects:** Applications for establishment, construction, installation, or expansion of battery energy storage systems or data centers; no named project identified
- **Detailed status:** Adopted. The Commission's own document repository shows the moratorium text moved from a 'generals' (draft/agenda-attachment) filing on 2026-04-15 to a 'regulations' filing dated 2026-05-20, and secondary press reports the Commission approved the moratorium following a public hearing in mid-May 2026. The operative text (Section 6) fixes a 12-month term running from the effective date of adoption, notwithstanding press descriptions of it as a 'two-year moratorium' (which do not match the adopted text I read).
- **Outcome:** Pending; moratorium directs the commission to prepare zoning amendments as appropriate

### New Haven

- **Type:** City
- **Status:** 🟡 Pending
- **Date enacted:** Not yet adopted as of 2026-07-06; proposed by Board of Alders Majority Leader Richard Furlow as a communication on the Monday Board of Alders agenda, to proceed next to an aldermanic committee for a public hearing before returning to the full board for a final vote.
- **Normalized date:** `—` (unverified)
- **Duration:** Proposed 12 months
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `ct-new-haven-undated`
- **Legal basis:** Proposed Board of Alders resolution/ordinance (introduced as a communication; not yet referred to committee as of 2026-07-06)
- **What prompted it:** Proactive/regulatory-gap: the city has no zoning framework for data centers and wants to develop one before any project is proposed, drawing on approaches used by Groton, Morris, and West Haven, Connecticut.
- **Affected projects:** None. New Haven's Deputy Director of Zoning stated there are no current proposals or plans by any entity to build a data center in New Haven.
- **Detailed status:** Pending; introduced 2026-07-06, awaiting aldermanic committee referral and public hearing before a final Board of Alders vote.
- **Outcome:** Proposed 12-month moratorium to allow the city's economic development department to convene a working group evaluating opportunities and impacts before any zoning framework is adopted.

### West Haven

- **Status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** 2026-06-08, per City Council meeting minutes
- **Normalized date:** `2026-06-08` (exact)
- **Duration:** 1 year

- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `ct-west-haven-2026`
- **Legal basis:** City Council resolution requiring a 1-year moratorium on the development of data centers, requested by Mayor Dorinda Borer
- **What prompted it:** Not detailed beyond the mayor's request in captured minutes
